The CodeBuddy session reads this committed copy. Push/publication, real Tencent app calls, key rotation and credential delivery are not authorized.

   6→

The public/judge release waits for separate publication and credential gates. Do not describe a local ZIP as an online demo link.

  12→
  13→### Allowed production files
  14→
  15→Create:
  16→
  17→- `tools/launch_live.py`
  18→- `start-live.bat`

  30→
  31→- `tests/test_w47_live_launcher.py`
  32→- `tests/test_w47_submission_package.py`
  33→- `tests/browser/w47_live_launcher.cjs`

  40→## Dispatch and Git protocol
  41→
  42→1. Read this brief, `CODEBUDDY.md`, the four acceptance files, and definitions of the existing server/config helpers they exercise. Read HEAD at runtime. The historical prep baseline is `4adbbbf30085a1132ee2b8e832f292c4f95f3252`; it is not a literal HEAD requirement after the RED/brief commit.
  43→2. Confirm the worktree is clean and the five new production paths are absent. Inspect the acceptance tests' exported helper interfaces and CLI/manifest assertions before choosing an implementation.
  44→3. Read only this worktree and installed runtime libraries. Do not read the planning repository, other worktrees, the scratch/reference implementations, real `.env`/`.env.live` files, credentials or account stores. Synthetic credential fixtures created by the acceptance tests are permitted.
  45→4. No cloud/app-model requests, external downloads, package installation, browser-account automation, merge, push, stash, reset, cleanup of another session, or broad deletion. Tests may use their synthetic fixtures and loopback listeners only. Never start a live Tencent server with actual keys.
  46→5. The parent pre-authorizes scoped Read/Glob/Grep/Edit/Write/Bash tools through process-local CLI settings. A denial is a stop condition, not permission to find a bypass. Do not modify permanent settings.
  47→6. If the operator has authorized the W47 build commit, stage only the six allowed production paths by name and commit only those. Never use `git add -A`, `git add .`, or commit tests/briefs. No merge or push. Report the branch commit and exact changed-path list.
  48→7. Give the parent the commands, counts, failures/errors/skips, wrapper mode/line-ending results, outstanding limits and the next reproducible step. Do not claim final review or live access succeeded; those are parent/recipient gates.
  49→
  50→## Live launcher contract
  51→
  52→### Credentials and endpoint
  53→
  54→- Default credential file is `<package-root>/.env.live`. Support explicit `--credentials PATH` and `--port PORT`. Default live port is 8030. Help must work without a credential file.
  55→- Use the existing application env parser for the selected file. Validate a UTF-8 text sidecar before exporting it. Refuse unreadable/invalid encoding, malformed assignments, unsupported variable names, duplicate names, absent/blank/placeholder role keys, and invalid endpoint values. Errors must not echo file contents, values, endpoints or constructor exception text.
  56→- Require `TENCENT_ADP_RIDER_APP_KEY`, `TENCENT_ADP_DRIVER_APP_KEY`, `TENCENT_ADP_JUDGE_APP_KEY`. The selected sidecar wins over stale process values. Do not read a legacy root `.env` or export arbitrary settings.
  57→- Pin the destination to `https://wss.lke.tencentcloud.com/adp/v2/chat`. An optional `TENCENT_ADP_ENDPOINT` sidecar entry must equal that reviewed destination. The shipped `app/config.json` `llm.endpoint` must also match. Refuse alternatives before constructing a provider.
  58→- Explicitly set the reviewed endpoint in this process before construction, including when the sidecar omits it. A stale inherited endpoint must not steer the client. Malformed URL parsing must return a plain refusal, not raise.
  59→- Do not print credentials or put them on command lines. Do not write to application config, create keys or rotate them.
  60→
  61→### Provider and server ownership
  62→
  63→- Call the existing `app.server.make_server` with explicit `provider="tencent"`. No fallback to mock, config-provider inheritance or new pipeline.
  64→- This launcher owns its own bound loopback server. Refuse an occupied port, even if the listener advertises the same application or is another live instance. Never reuse a listener or open its page as if it belonged to this process.
  65→- Verify the bound server's in-process provider is Tencent before opening a browser. If wrong, close it and refuse. Readiness precedes browser launch.
  66→- Open `/party/`; print operator-console and status URLs with the actual chosen port. A browser-opening failure must leave useful manual URLs, not silently kill the owned server.
  67→- Keep the server in the owning process. Ctrl+C shuts it down and calls `server_close`; closing a browser tab does not. Redact provider startup errors with fixed value-free text.
  68→
  69→### Wrappers
  70→
  71→- Windows `start-live.bat`: CRLF, correct quoting for paths with spaces, package cwd, Python 3.9+ using `py -3` with an appropriate `python` fallback, and readable failure text.
  72→- Mac `start-live.command`: executable mode, quoted package cwd, Python 3.9+ check, and invocation of the live helper. No global security changes.
  73→- Do not modify or replace `start.bat`, `start.command` or `tools/launch.py`.
  74→- There is no Windows execution claim yet. Actual new-live-launcher execution on the teammate's Windows machine is a later handoff gate.
  75→
  76→## Source packager contract
  77→
  78→- CLI selects `--repo`, an explicit committed `--revision`, required `--purpose rehearsal|submission`, and `--out`. Output filename is `ryde-live-<purpose>-<12-hex-source-revision>.zip`; the archive has that single root folder.
  79→- Inventory the selected Git tree and read its blobs. Do not recursively ZIP the development folder or collect untracked local files. Refuse tracked modifications and ambiguous/invalid source revision.
  80→- Require the live helper, both live wrappers, instructions and preserved source entry points in the selected revision. Validate wrapper modes/CRLF, not just filename presence.
  81→- Refuse tracked credential paths case-insensitively, filled credential examples, detected secret-shaped content, escaping/looping symlinks, Git LFS pointers, malformed/nonportable paths, case-fold collisions and unsafe output destinations. Failure writes no archive, does not overwrite an existing archive and leaves no partial ZIP.
  82→- Check disk identity for output containment, including existing parents and case aliases. Path spelling or `resolve()` alone is insufficient on the default Mac filesystem. Cover Windows-style backslashes, drive names, reserved names and trailing dot/space components.
  83→- Omit and record permitted junk such as run output, caches, editor locks, local CodeBuddy settings and OS files. Do not silently omit a tracked credential and call the source safe.
  84→- Scan paths and source content. Secret-test fixtures must keep identical runtime values without embedding literal scanner-triggering tokens/headers into their distributed test source. Do not weaken the scanner to package tests.
  85→- Include `MANIFEST.json` with the tested schema: exact source revision, purpose, included path/mode/hash records, excluded path/reason records, counts and narrow scan limitations. Match the supplied tests' field and helper interfaces.
  86→- Keep complete source, tests and evidence subject to the separate release gate. Do not perform a privacy/history scrub or claim the scan proves absence of every real credential. A parent-owned comparison against actual key bytes remains a distribution gate.
  87→- Two packages from the same revision must have matching extracted inventories/content hashes. Preserve executable Mac mode and Windows CRLF in ZIP entries and after normal OS extraction.
  88→
  89→## Instructions and filming handoff
  90→
  91→`docs/live-copy.md` explains extraction, Python 3.9+, internet, the privately delivered `.env.live`, live versus mock entry points, the terminal's lifetime, printed URLs, manual commands and narrowly scoped OS script-warning remedies. No package or instructions carry actual keys.
  92→
  93→The operator uses synthetic inputs, keeps run references/provider evidence, coordinates one live caller at a time across machines, and preserves locally saved runs across restarts. Describe real model waits and provider errors without promising an outcome. A decision record does not transfer money.
  94→
  95→Explain the agreed no-show and above-cap rehearsal pair. Do not invite unlimited retries or silently broaden the two-rehearsal-filing allowance. Stop for the operator if the real result differs from the filming narrative; do not replace it with mock output or narrate a planned ending.
  96→
  97→The accepted recording script is the planning-side `drafts/w26/demo-script.md`, target 6:30, delivered separately by the operator. `tools/deployment/demo-video-script.md`, target 7:25, is an older build-repository script retained in the complete-source ZIP. Its inclusion does not approve it for filming. State that it is an included source file, and that the accepted recording script is a separate teammate handoff. Do not remove the older source file or tell the recipient both scripts are outside the ZIP. Their filming edit must be settled before production footage.
  98→
  99→Label shortened waits and saved-run replay honestly. Never film credentials or account consoles. A rehearsal package is private, not public-release clearance. Judge delivery waits for release scrub/history/secret checks, verified access, approved private credential channel and form requirements.
 100→
 101→## Verification protocol
 102→
 103→Use `env -u PYTHONPATH /usr/bin/python3 -B` on this Mac. The parent supplies an existing writable TMPDIR. Do not create files under `/tmp` or copy stale browser paths. Clear `W47_BASELINE_TREE` for builder checks; that opt-in baseline archive check belongs to the parent.

 111→Then implement only the allowed files and run that same command to GREEN. Report the two deliberately disabled baseline checks as skips rather than hiding them. No application network/model call is required.

 113→A single full-suite discovery took over ten minutes in parent verification. Do not require it to fit one short foreground tool call. Run any broader builder regression checks in bounded module/class groups with the same interpreter and environment, record every group's result, and let the parent perform the authoritative single-process full suite with the browser/opt-in environment on a frozen branch archive. A timeout is not a test result. Stop rather than modifying code for tests you did not complete.
 114→
 115→The parent re-aims mutation literals at the actual CodeBuddy implementation, requires each planted defect to cause an assertion failure with no test errors, checks frozen-file byte preservation and the real browser at narrow/desktop widths, then verifies the actual extracted branch ZIP. The reference's mutation search strings are not a battery for rewritten code.
 116→
 117→### Measured prep evidence, not a future branch claim
 118→
 119→On the combined scratch reference extracted from its own ZIP:
 120→
 121→- Full suite: 1817 tests, zero failures/errors/skips.
 122→- Unmodified application baseline plus the same acceptance files: 1817 tests, 116 expected failures, zero errors/skips. Breakdown: live launcher 61, packager 54, old intro expectation 1.
 123→- Browser: 7 checks passed at 390px and 1280px, using mock runtime only.
 124→- Planted defects: launcher 30, packager 19, parent additions 3. All 52 caught, no survivors or test errors. A separate equivalent-rewrite control correctly stayed green.
 125→- Actual ZIP: 498 included source files plus manifest; one editor lock omitted. Every included hash/byte matched reference source; normal Mac extraction preserved executable mode/CRLF in a spaces-and-Unicode path.
 126→
 127→After that run, parent archive inspection exposed incorrect handoff wording: the old 7:25 script is a build-side source file and is actually included. A new assertion first failed on the old instructions, then the candidate instructions were corrected without changing launcher/packager code. The corrected candidate subsequently passed the full extracted suite at 1818 tests, zero failures/errors/skips. Focused baseline RED was 174 tests with 117 expected assertion failures, zero errors/skips, exactly the prior 116 failures plus this instruction pin. Reverting the instruction correction failed the new pin with clean start/end controls. Runtime source bytes remained identical to the earlier mutation-verified implementation. Re-derive these counts on the actual build branch. The brief itself also adds a source file, so future archive counts must be derived, not copied from the earlier measurement. Parent evidence is a feasibility/pinning proof, not proof that the unbuilt production branch is ready.
 128→
 129→## Stop conditions and completion
 130→
 131→Stop for any unexpected file edit, conflict with a protected byte/hash, denied tool, wrong served model, exposure of a real credential, missing interface, need for paid app-model requests, or proposed policy/outcome change. Never bypass the gate.
 132→
 133→Builder done means its allowed files are implemented, its focused tests are green, wrapper bytes/modes are correct, the source diff stays within the exact allowed list, and it reports honest regression coverage and a scoped branch commit. Parent full verification, GLM 5.3 review, live-account checks, real extracted-package filings, private delivery and new Windows execution remain separate gates. No push or credential handoff follows from builder completion.

1→# PROJECT: Ryde — Multi-Agent Autonomous Dispute Resolution
   2→
   3→**Status: BUILT, IN POLISH (updated 2026-10-07).** The system runs end to end on the mock and on
   4→the real Tencent model; the application build freezes on **12 Oct 2026** (operator ruling), after
   5→which only recording, documentation and deploy work continue. Building started 2026-09-21. Planning closed **2026-09-19** and the scope, stack and
   6→workflow are ruled. This file is CodeBuddy's memory for this project: the builder's entry
   7→point. The ruled scope lives in
   8→the planning repository and is deliberately unreadable from here (the permission fence in
   9→`.codebuddy/settings.json` denies reads of that path, and it is verified to work), so
  10→**everything you need is in this file, `docs/` and the kickoff prompt the operator gives you**.
  11→If a session needs a fact that is neither here nor in the docs: stop and ask; do not invent
  12→scope.
  13→
  14→## What this project is
  15→
  16→Ryde track entry for the Tencent Cloud "AI CAN DO IT" Hackathon Singapore 2026. The challenge is a
  17→**multi-agent autonomous dispute resolution system** for ride-hailing disputes: a Rider Advocate
  18→agent, a Driver Advocate agent, and a Judge agent that weighs both cases, applies company policy and
  19→issues a ruling with a confidence score.
  20→
  21→`docs/statement-extract.md` holds the challenge statement verbatim. Read it before any build work.
  22→It is the requirements floor: the locked scope below is the team's chosen subset of it, and the
  23→locked scope never widens past the statement.
  24→
  25→## Hard requirements (non-negotiable)
  26→
  27→- The project must be **original** and built on **at least one of CodeBuddy or WorkBuddy**.
  28→- **Proof of product usage is mandatory.** Without it the project is **not scored at all**. Evidence
  29→  is screenshots of CodeBuddy/WorkBuddy chat logs, minimum three, accumulated as work happens. It
  30→  cannot be reconstructed later, so capture as you go.
  31→- The project must be **demoable end to end for at least two dispute categories**.
  32→- **Inter-agent communication must be observable** to a judge: a visible log or UI showing how the
  33→  agents exchange information and build their cases.
  34→- Deliverables include a public GitHub repo with complete source, an architecture diagram, and a live
  35→  demo walkthrough.
  36→- The repository is **PUBLIC**. Never commit credentials, API keys, tokens or personal data.
  37→
  38→## Locked build scope
  39→
  40→These decisions are ruled by the team and are **not open to re-litigation**:
  41→
  42→- **Categories:** route deviation + no-show charge, end to end. No third category.
  43→- **Agents:** exactly three decide each dispute — Rider Advocate, Driver Advocate, Judge. The
  44→  Judge always emits a confidence score (0–1). Below a configurable threshold it does not rule;
  45→  the parties see only a neutral "your case is still under review" message. Escalation is MVP, not stretch.
  46→  *(Amended 2026-10-01.)* A fourth role, the **Policy & Precedent agent**, is a stretch item
  47→  built only if time allows: it reads human decisions and **proposes** policy changes, a human
  48→  approves or rejects each proposal, and it **never rules on a live case** and never edits the
  49→  policy or the code gates itself.
  50→- **Parties are spectators:** disputes arrive through a standardized intake form (category
  51→  dropdown; "other" routes to a human-review queue with a neutral message). The advocates screen
  52→  the submitted answers and may ask the party targeted follow-ups only when data conflicts or
  53→  is insufficient. No fourth intake agent. Parties never chat with the agents.
  54→- **Deterministic evidence layer:** all quantitative evidence (route deviation km/%, duration vs
  55→  estimate, fare recomputation, cancellation timestamps, chat-log signals, behaviour profile)
  56→  is computed in Python into a typed **Evidence Pack**. Agents may cite pack fields; they must
  57→  never do the arithmetic themselves.
  58→- **Policy as a swappable document:** `docs/policy.md`, rules with IDs and machine-checkable
  59→  preconditions, provenance stated in the file. The Judge and advocates cite rule IDs. A real
  60→  organiser version, if one ever arrives, drops in with no code change.
  61→- **Dataset as a swappable document:** synthesised corpus in `data/`, labelled with
  62→  ground-truth rulings (the correct ruling per case, by design) so replayed-run consistency is
  63→  measurable. Same swap rule.
  64→- **Observability surface (required by the statement):** a case-file view — each side's claim,
  65→  evidence and policy citations, with agent-to-agent traffic as a compact timestamped event
  66→  strip (full text one click deeper). This screen is the demo's home.
  67→- **Stack:** Python backend + plain HTML/JS front end. No heavy framework. The backend calls
  68→  Tencent Cloud's LLM API directly (key in `.env`, never committed). CodeBuddy writes the code;
  69→  it is never the runtime.
  70→- **Repo layout:** `app/` (Python backend), `ui/` (front end), `docs/` (architecture diagram,
  71→  policy set, dataset description), `evidence/` (development-process screenshots), `tools/` +
  72→  `tests/` (marked **non-app**: helper scripts and tests only; `app/` and `ui/` never import
  73→  from them). **The repo is PUBLIC at submission — never commit credentials or personal data.**
  74→- **Deployment:** local run for the live demo (real backend, real LLM calls). *(Amended
  75→  2026-10-01.)* The public link is a static replay on EdgeOne Pages of the **full loop** (filing →
  76→  the Judge withholds → a human decides → the party's status page), labelled honestly as a
  77→  replay of a real run with its date; it ships first. Optional polish on top: a hosted live
  78→  system behind one shared judge password (every page and API), a daily case cap and a daily
  79→  health check, with keys rotated before it goes up.
  80→
  81→## Non-negotiable engineering rules
  82→
  83→- Never commit `.env`, API keys, tokens, or any credential. The repo is public.
  84→- Do not read or write anything outside this folder — **this is a rule you must honour, not
  85→  something the fence guarantees.** The permission fence in `.codebuddy/settings.json` denies
  86→  reads of the planning repository path and of secret files (`.env`, `*.pem`, `*.key`,
  87→  `secrets/`), denies `curl`, `wget`, `rm -rf` and `git push`, and asks before `git remote`.
  88→  It does NOT block other writes or other reads. Staying inside this folder is your job.
  89→- Verify work by running it, not by describing it. A feature is done when it has been exercised and
  90→  the real output checked.
  91→- Keep the demo path working at all times. A half-built stretch goal that breaks the main flow is
  92→  worse than no stretch goal.
  93→- **Only the CodeBuddy build lane writes `app/` and `ui/`.** Any other AI assistant used for
  94→  rescue or unblocking (e.g. another coding agent) is confined to `tools/` and `tests/` and must never
  95→  touch application code — the project's "built on CodeBuddy" claim must stay honest.
  96→  *(Amended 2026-10-01.)* A defect that lives only in `app/` or `ui/` follows the normal path:
  97→  the planning agent writes a failing test and a brief, the CodeBuddy build lane fixes it (on
  98→  the default flash model), the planning agent verifies. **One exception:** within 48 hours of
  99→  the submission deadline, if the build lane cannot land a fix in time, the rescue lane may fix
 100→  it, and every such change is logged with its reason in the commit message and in
 101→  `docs/tool-experiences.md`.
 102→
 103→## How work is done here
 104→
 105→- **One capability at a time**, verified before moving on.
 106→- Commit with a clear message after each verified step.
 107→- Log decisions as they are made. A future session starts from these files, not from memory.
 108→- **Effort follows the Demo Day rubric:** 40 of 100 points are story, design and presentation,
 109→  so `README.md`, `docs/architecture.md` and the demo walkthrough are deliverables on the same
 110→  footing as code — polished after the MVP floor is standing, never skipped.
 111→- **Run from this folder.** `cd ~/hermes-workspace/projects/ryde-build && codebuddy`. Sessions are
 112→  scoped by launch directory, and this folder carries its own memory file and permission fence.
 113→- **Default model is `deepseek-v4.1-flash`** (global default, x0.00 cost multiplier). Override per
 114→  task with `--model <id>` only when the work warrants the expense: GPT-5.6-Luna x0.14 is the cheap
 115→  upgrade, Kimi-K3 x1.62 for hard reasoning. Never use Primary, Deep, Sol or GPT-6-Astra here.
 116→- **Headless capture:** `codebuddy -p "<prompt>" --output-format json` returns machine-readable
 117→  results and writes a transcript to `~/.codebuddy/projects/`. Useful when the build needs to be
 118→  driven from outside the interactive session.
 119→
 120→## Layout
 121→
 122→```
 123→ryde-build/
 124→├── CODEBUDDY.md            # this file — project memory + locked scope
 125→├── README.md               # judge's entry point (judge-first: what it is → see it run → diagram)
 126→├── .codebuddy/
 127→│   └── settings.json       # permission fence
 128→├── app/                    # Python backend — agents, evidence layer, LLM calls, server, eval
 129→├── ui/                     # plain HTML/JS front end — operator console (case-file view)
 130→│   └── party/              # rider and driver intake forms, driver account, status page
 131→├── data/packs/             # two swappable dataset packs, ground-truth labelled:
 132→│                           #   organiser-style-v1 (default) and ryde-synth-v1
 133→├── docs/
 134→│   ├── statement-extract.md  # challenge statement, verbatim — the only requirements source
 135→│   ├── policy.md             # policy rule set (swappable; provenance stated in-file)
 136→│   ├── dataset.md            # dataset description + provenance
 137→│   ├── architecture.md       # required deliverable: diagram + system description
 138→│   ├── prompts.md            # how the prompts drive each agent
 139→│   ├── replay.md             # static replay export for the public link
 140→│   ├── evidence-plan.md      # §8 evidence rules and naming
 141→│   ├── tool-experiences.md   # running log of how the tools behaved
 142→│   └── build-briefs/         # one brief per build session, kept as a process record
 143→├── evidence/               # §8 screenshots (YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<topic>.png|.jpg)
 144→├── tools/                  # NON-APP helper scripts — app/ never imports from here
 145→│   └── replay/             # static replay page and its shim
 146→└── tests/                  # NON-APP tests (stdlib only)
 147→```
 148→
 149→New session briefs go in `docs/build-briefs/`. Do not create a document as a side effect of
 150→other work; each one is authored in the session whose brief names it.
 151→

1→"""The LLM interface every adapter implements, plus JSON-response parsing.
   2→
   3→One method: `complete(request) -> LLMResponse`. That is the whole contract, so an
   4→adapter can be swapped without touching agent logic.
   5→"""
   6→
   7→from __future__ import annotations
   8→
   9→import abc
  10→import hashlib
  11→import json
  12→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
  13→from typing import Any, Dict, Optional
  14→
  15→
  16→class LLMError(RuntimeError):
  17→    """The provider could not be reached, is misconfigured, or returned an error."""
  18→
  19→
  20→class LLMTransientError(LLMError):
  21→    """The provider failure may clear when the same call is tried again."""
  22→
  23→
  24→class LLMContractError(LLMError):
  25→    """The provider responded, but not with the JSON object the agent contract requires."""
  26→
  27→
  28→@dataclass(frozen=True)
  29→class LLMRequest:
  30→    """One prompt to one agent.
  31→
  32→    agent            which agent is asking ("rider_advocate", "driver_advocate", "judge")
  33→    system_prompt    role, output contract and hard rules
  34→    user_prompt      the case material: dispute intake, Evidence Pack, policy document
  35→    metadata         adapter-facing hints. Real adapters ignore it; the mock uses it to
  36→                     build deterministic responses. Never carries anything that is not
  37→                     already in the prompts.
  38→    """
  39→
  40→    agent: str
  41→    system_prompt: str
  42→    user_prompt: str
  43→    expect_json: bool = True
  44→    metadata: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
  45→    timeout_seconds: Optional[float] = None
  46→
  47→    def fingerprint(self) -> str:
  48→        """Stable hash of the prompts — recorded with the case so a run is reproducible."""
  49→        digest = hashlib.sha256()
  50→        digest.update(self.agent.encode("utf-8"))
  51→        digest.update(b"\x00")
  52→        digest.update(self.system_prompt.encode("utf-8"))
  53→        digest.update(b"\x00")
  54→        digest.update(self.user_prompt.encode("utf-8"))
  55→        return digest.hexdigest()[:16]
  56→
  57→
  58→@dataclass(frozen=True)
  59→class LLMResponse:
  60→    """What came back, plus enough provenance to log it honestly."""
  61→
  62→    text: str
  63→    provider: str
  64→    model: str
  65→    usage: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
  66→    finish_reason: Optional[str] = None
  67→
  68→    def as_log_fields(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
  69→        return {
  70→            "provider": self.provider,
  71→            "model": self.model,
  72→            "usage": self.usage,
  73→            "finish_reason": self.finish_reason,
  74→        }
  75→
  76→
  77→class LLMClient(abc.ABC):
  78→    """Interface every LLM adapter implements."""
  79→
  80→    provider_name = "unknown"
  81→
  82→    @abc.abstractmethod
  83→    def complete(self, request: LLMRequest) -> LLMResponse:
  84→        """Run one prompt. Raises LLMError on transport/config failure."""
  85→        raise NotImplementedError
  86→
  87→
  88→def parse_json_object(text: str, *, agent: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
  89→    """Parse the JSON object an agent contract requires out of a model response.
  90→
  91→    Tolerates the two things models actually do: wrapping the object in a ```json
  92→    fence, and adding a sentence before or after it. Anything else is a hard failure —
  93→    a malformed response must never be silently repaired into a ruling.
  94→    """
  95→    if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():
  96→        raise LLMContractError("%s: model returned an empty response" % agent)
  97→
  98→    candidate = text.strip()
  99→
 100→    # Strip a fenced code block if the whole response is wrapped in one.
 101→    if candidate.startswith("```"):
 102→        body = candidate.split("\n", 1)[1] if "\n" in candidate else ""
 103→        if body.rstrip().endswith("```"):
 104→            body = body.rstrip()[: -len("```")]
 105→        candidate = body.strip()
 106→
 107→    try:
 108→        parsed = json.loads(candidate)
 109→    except json.JSONDecodeError:
 110→        start = candidate.find("{")
 111→        end = candidate.rfind("}")
 112→        if start == -1 or end == -1 or end <= start:
 113→            raise LLMContractError(
 114→                "%s: no JSON object found in model response: %r" % (agent, text[:400])
 115→            )
 116→        try:
 117→            parsed = json.loads(candidate[start : end + 1])
 118→        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
 119→            raise LLMContractError(
 120→                "%s: model response is not valid JSON (%s): %r" % (agent, exc, text[:400])
 121→            ) from exc
 122→
 123→    if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
 124→        raise LLMContractError(
 125→            "%s: expected a JSON object, got %s" % (agent, type(parsed).__name__)
 126→        )
 127→    return parsed
 128→

1→"""Tencent Cloud ADP adapter: the real LLM provider.
   2→
   3→The three agents are three published Tencent Cloud ADP (Agent Development Platform)
   4→apps, one per role: Ryde Rider Advocate, Ryde Driver Advocate and Ryde Judge. Each app
   5→carries only a short role card. This code still sends the full role prompt on every
   6→call, so the repo stays the source of truth for what each agent is told, and every gate
   7→that moves money stays in Python.
   8→
   9→Protocol (checked against the live endpoint on 2026-09-28):
  10→
  11→- ``POST <llm.endpoint>`` with a JSON body. The app's AppKey travels in the body; there
  12→  is no auth header and no request signing.
  13→- The reply is Server-Sent Events even with ``"Stream": "disable"``. The answer is in
  14→  the ``response.completed`` event, at ``Response.Messages[Type=reply].Contents[].Text``.
  15→- ADP reports errors as an ``error`` event inside an HTTP 200. The status code alone
  16→  never proves success.
  17→- Tencent's web firewall sits in front of the endpoint. A blocked request never
  18→  reaches ADP: it comes back as HTTP 501 with an HTML redirect to
  19→  ``waf-captcha.cloud.tencent.com``. The trigger is prompt content (backticks together
  20→  with ASCII brackets), not size, so every prompt is cleaned before sending
  21→  (``clean_for_firewall``).
  22→- The free plan allows 10 calls a minute, so calls are spaced at least
  23→  ``MIN_CALL_INTERVAL_SECONDS`` apart.
  24→
  25→Failures are classified here and raised once; the retry loop lives in the agent layer.
  26→There is no fallback to the mock. An error message names the cause (the status code, the
  27→ADP error code, the kind of failure) but never carries a response body, and every configured
  28→AppKey is redacted from it, so a key can never reach a terminal, a log or a case file through
  29→an error.
  30→"""
  31→
  32→from __future__ import annotations
  33→
  34→import http.client
  35→import json
  36→import threading
  37→import time
  38→import urllib.error
  39→import urllib.request
  40→import uuid
  41→from typing import Any, Dict, Mapping, Optional
  42→
  43→from ..config import LLMSettings, read_secret
  44→from .base import LLMClient, LLMContractError, LLMError, LLMRequest, LLMResponse, LLMTransientError
  45→
  46→#: One ADP app per agent. The environment variable holds that app's AppKey.
  47→APP_KEY_ENV_VARS = {
  48→    "rider_advocate": "TENCENT_ADP_RIDER_APP_KEY",
  49→    "driver_advocate": "TENCENT_ADP_DRIVER_APP_KEY",
  50→    "judge": "TENCENT_ADP_JUDGE_APP_KEY",
  51→}
  52→ENDPOINT_ENV_VAR = "TENCENT_ADP_ENDPOINT"
  53→
  54→#: The free plan allows 10 calls per minute. 6.5 s between call starts stays under it.
  55→MIN_CALL_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 6.5
  56→
  57→#: Sent as the ADP VisitorId. Each call also gets a fresh ConversationId, so no agent
  58→#: ever shares conversation context with another agent or with an earlier call.
  59→VISITOR_ID = "ryde-dispute-system"
  60→
  61→#: Values left in app/config.json until the endpoint is set. Calling with any of these
  62→#: still present is a configuration error.
  63→PLACEHOLDER_MARKERS = ("TODO-pin", "example/v1")
  64→
  65→#: The firewall blocks prompts where backticks and ASCII brackets occur together. The
  66→#: model reads the full-width forms exactly as it reads the ASCII ones.
  67→FIREWALL_SAFE_CHARACTERS = str.maketrans(
  68→    {
  69→        "`": None,
  70→        "(": "\uff08",
  71→        ")": "\uff09",
  72→        "<": "\uff1c",
  73→        ">": "\uff1e",
  74→        ";": "\uff1b",
  75→        "|": "\uff5c",
  76→        "$": "\uff04",
  77→    }
  78→)
  79→FIREWALL_MARKER = "waf-captcha"
  80→
  81→#: A Judge-sized reply measured 89 KB on the live endpoint (it echoes the prompt). A
  82→#: response larger than this is refused rather than read into memory.
  83→MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024
  84→REDACTED = "<redacted>"
  85→
  86→
  87→def clean_for_firewall(text: str) -> str:
  88→    """Drop backticks and swap ( ) < > ; | $ for their full-width forms."""
  89→    return text.translate(FIREWALL_SAFE_CHARACTERS)
  90→
  91→
  92→class TencentLLMClient(LLMClient):
  93→    """Calls the ADP app that belongs to the requesting agent. See the module docstring."""
  94→
  95→    provider_name = "tencent"
  96→
  97→    def __init__(
  98→        self,
  99→        settings: LLMSettings,
 100→        app_keys: Optional[Mapping[str, str]] = None,
 101→        min_interval_seconds: float = MIN_CALL_INTERVAL_SECONDS,
 102→        **_ignored: Any,
 103→    ):
 104→        self.settings = settings
 105→        self.endpoint = read_secret(ENDPOINT_ENV_VAR) or settings.endpoint
 106→        self.model = settings.model
 107→        if app_keys is None:
 108→            app_keys = {agent: read_secret(var) for agent, var in APP_KEY_ENV_VARS.items()}
 109→        self._app_keys = {agent: (app_keys.get(agent) or "") for agent in APP_KEY_ENV_VARS}
 110→        self.min_interval_seconds = float(min_interval_seconds)
 111→        self._pace_lock = threading.Lock()
 112→        self._last_call_started: Optional[float] = None
 113→        self._check_configuration()
 114→
 115→    def _check_configuration(self) -> None:
 116→        """Fail loudly and early. Never a silent fallback to the mock."""
 117→        missing = [APP_KEY_ENV_VARS[agent] for agent, key in self._app_keys.items() if not key]
 118→        if missing:
 119→            raise LLMError(
 120→                "missing ADP app key(s): %s. Put them in .env (see .env.example) or export "
 121→                "them. To run without keys, use --llm mock." % ", ".join(missing)
 122→            )
 123→        if not self.endpoint or any(marker in self.endpoint for marker in PLACEHOLDER_MARKERS):
 124→            raise LLMError("llm.endpoint is not set (%r); see app/config.json." % (self.endpoint,))
 125→        if not self.model or any(marker in self.model for marker in PLACEHOLDER_MARKERS):
 126→            raise LLMError("llm.model is not set (%r); see app/config.json." % (self.model,))
 127→
 128→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ interface
 129→
 130→    def complete(self, request: LLMRequest) -> LLMResponse:
 131→        app_key = [REDACTED_SECRET](request.agent)
 132→        if not app_key:
 133→            raise LLMError("no ADP app is configured for agent %r" % (request.agent,))
 134→        body = self._build_body(request, app_key)
 135→        self._pace()
 136→        try:
 137→            status, text = self._post(body, request.timeout_seconds)
 138→            return self._parse_events(status, text)
 139→        except LLMError as exc:
 140→            raise type(exc)(self._redact(str(exc))) from None
 141→
 142→    def _redact(self, message: str) -> str:
 143→        """Remove every configured AppKey from a message before it leaves this class."""
 144→        for key in self._app_keys.values():
 145→            if key:
 146→                message = message.replace(key, REDACTED)
 147→        return message
 148→
 149→    # ------------------------------------------------------------ request / response
 150→
 151→    def _build_body(self, request: LLMRequest, app_key: str) -> bytes:
 152→        prompt = (
 153→            "SYSTEM INSTRUCTIONS (follow exactly):\n"
 154→            + request.system_prompt
 155→            + "\n\n---\nINPUT:\n"
 156→            + request.user_prompt
 157→        )
 158→        payload = {
 159→            "RequestId": str(uuid.uuid4()),
 160→            "ConversationId": str(uuid.uuid4()),
 161→            "AppKey": app_key,
 162→            "VisitorId": VISITOR_ID,
 163→            "Contents": [{"Type": "text", "Text": clean_for_firewall(prompt)}],
 164→            "Incremental": False,
 165→            "Stream": "disable",
 166→        }
 167→        return json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")
 168→
 169→    def _pace(self) -> None:
 170→        """Hold the call until MIN interval has passed since the previous call started."""
 171→        with self._pace_lock:
 172→            now = time.monotonic()
 173→            if self._last_call_started is not None:
 174→                wait = self._last_call_started + self.min_interval_seconds - now
 175→                if wait > 0:
 176→                    time.sleep(wait)
 177→                    now = time.monotonic()
 178→            self._last_call_started = now
 179→
 180→    def _post(self, body: bytes, request_timeout: Optional[float] = None):
 181→        timeout = float(self.settings.timeout_seconds)
 182→        if request_timeout is not None:
 183→            timeout = max(1.0, min(timeout, float(request_timeout)))
 184→        http_request = urllib.request.Request(
 185→            self.endpoint,
 186→            data=body,
 187→            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "Accept": "text/event-stream"},
 188→            method="POST",
 189→        )
 190→        try:
 191→            with urllib.request.urlopen(  # noqa: S310 - endpoint comes from config
 192→                http_request, timeout=timeout
 193→            ) as response:
 194→                return response.status, self._read_body(response)
 195→        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
 196→            try:
 197→                raw = exc.read(MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES + 1)
 198→            except (http.client.HTTPException, OSError):
 199→                raw = b""
 200→            if exc.code == 501 or FIREWALL_MARKER.encode("ascii") in raw:
 201→                raise LLMError(
 202→                    "the Tencent web firewall blocked the request (HTTP %s); it never "
 203→                    "reached ADP" % exc.code
 204→                ) from None
 205→            # The body is deliberately left out: an error page can echo the request.
 206→            error_type = LLMTransientError if exc.code == 429 or 500 <= exc.code < 600 else LLMError
 207→            raise error_type("ADP call failed: HTTP %s" % exc.code) from None
 208→        except http.client.HTTPException as exc:
 209→            raise LLMTransientError(
 210→                "ADP call failed: the connection broke while reading the reply (%s)"
 211→                % type(exc).__name__
 212→            ) from None
 213→        except (urllib.error.URLError, OSError) as exc:
 214→            reason = getattr(exc, "reason", exc)
 215→            kind = type(reason).__name__ if isinstance(reason, BaseException) else "network error"
 216→            raise LLMTransientError("ADP call failed: cannot reach the endpoint (%s)" % kind) from None
 217→
 218→    @staticmethod
 219→    def _read_body(response) -> str:
 220→        raw = response.read(MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES + 1)
 221→        if len(raw) > MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES:
 222→            raise LLMContractError("ADP reply is too large (over %d bytes)" % MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES)
 223→        try:
 224→            return raw.decode("utf-8")
 225→        except UnicodeDecodeError:
 226→            raise LLMContractError("ADP reply is not valid UTF-8") from None
 227→
 228→    def _parse_events(self, status: int, text: str) -> LLMResponse:
 229→        if FIREWALL_MARKER in text:
 230→            raise LLMError(
 231→                "the Tencent web firewall blocked the request (HTTP %s); it never reached ADP"
 232→                % status
 233→            )
 234→        completed = None
 235→        # SSE lines may end in CRLF, LF or CR; frames end at a blank line.
 236→        text = text.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")
 237→        for block in text.split("\n\n"):
 238→            data = "\n".join(
 239→                line[len("data:"):].strip()
 240→                for line in block.splitlines()
 241→                if line.startswith("data:")
 242→            )
 243→            if not data:
 244→                continue
 245→            try:
 246→                event = json.loads(data)
 247→            except json.JSONDecodeError:
 248→                continue  # the closing "data: [DONE]" frame, or noise
 249→            if not isinstance(event, dict):
 250→                continue
 251→            if event.get("Type") == "error":
 252→                error = event.get("Error") if isinstance(event.get("Error"), dict) else {}
 253→                raise LLMError(
 254→                    "ADP returned error %s: %s" % (error.get("Code"), error.get("Message"))
 255→                )
 256→            if event.get("Type") == "response.completed":
 257→                completed = event.get("Response")
 258→
 259→        if not isinstance(completed, dict):
 260→            raise LLMContractError("ADP sent no response.completed event (HTTP %s)" % status)
 261→        messages = completed.get("Messages")
 262→        replies = []
 263→        if isinstance(messages, list):
 264→            replies = [m for m in messages if isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("Type") == "reply"]
 265→        # Every reply message, in order: a reply split across messages is joined, not cut.
 266→        contents = [m.get("Contents") for m in replies if isinstance(m.get("Contents"), list)]
 267→        if not contents:
 268→            raise LLMContractError("ADP response.completed carries no reply message")
 269→        answer = "".join(
 270→            part.get("Text", "")
 271→            for parts in contents
 272→            for part in parts
 273→            if isinstance(part, dict) and part.get("Type") == "text" and isinstance(part.get("Text"), str)
 274→        )
 275→        if not answer.strip():
 276→            raise LLMContractError("ADP reply is empty")
 277→
 278→        usage: Dict[str, Any] = {}
 279→        stat = completed.get("StatInfo")
 280→        if isinstance(stat, dict):
 281→            tokens = stat.get("TotalTokens")
 282→            if isinstance(tokens, int) and not isinstance(tokens, bool):
 283→                usage["total_tokens"] = tokens
 284→
 285→        return LLMResponse(
 286→            text=answer,
 287→            provider=self.provider_name,
 288→            model=self.model,
 289→            usage=usage,
 290→            finish_reason=str(completed.get("Status") or "") or None,
 291→        )
 292→

1→"""One-click launcher for the Ryde demo.
   2→
   3→Double-clicked through start.command (macOS) or start.bat (Windows), or run by hand:
   4→
   5→    python3 tools/launch.py [--ports FIRST-LAST]
   6→
   7→The launcher picks the first free port in the range — reusing a Ryde demo that is
   8→already running — then runs the EXISTING app.server entry point in this same process
   9→with the mock provider, and opens the start page once the server answers. One process
  10→is load-bearing: Ctrl+C reaches app.server's own KeyboardInterrupt handler, and
  11→closing the terminal window (SIGHUP) ends the process and frees the port.
  12→
  13→This is a helper for the demo, not part of the app: app/ and ui/ never import it.
  14→"""
  15→
  16→from __future__ import annotations
  17→
  18→import argparse
  19→import errno
  20→import socket
  21→import sys
  22→import threading
  23→import time
  24→import urllib.error
  25→import urllib.request
  26→import webbrowser
  27→from pathlib import Path
  28→from typing import Optional, Tuple
  29→
  30→#: Run as `python3 tools/launch.py`, sys.path[0] is tools/, so the repository root
  31→#: goes in before app.server is imported. The launcher never re-implements server
  32→#: startup; it calls the existing entry point.
  33→REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
  34→if str(REPO_ROOT) not in sys.path:
  35→    sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))
  36→
  37→import app.server as server  # noqa: E402 - sys.path is prepared just above
  38→
  39→FIRST_PORT = 8000
  40→LAST_PORT = 8010
  41→START_PATH = "/start/"
  42→
  43→#: How long one probe may wait for an answer: a listener that accepts the connection
  44→#: but never speaks must not stall the launcher.
  45→PROBE_TIMEOUT = 1.0
  46→#: How long a refused loopback connect may take before it counts as busy. Windows
  47→#: retries a refusal for a second or two, so a shorter wait would read every free
  48→#: port as taken there.
  49→CONNECT_TIMEOUT = 3.0
  50→#: The browser waiter's polling cadence, and how long it waits for the server to
  51→#: answer before printing the URL instead.
  52→POLL_SECONDS = 0.1
  53→READY_TIMEOUT = 30.0
  54→
  55→#: The banner app/server.py sends. A 200 carrying it is the only proof that a port
  56→#: serves this demo and not some other program.
  57→SERVER_HEADER = "RydePartyServer/"
  58→
  59→#: Every loopback probe goes through this opener, which ignores the user's proxy
  60→#: settings: urllib honours http_proxy and the system proxy, and macOS's default
  61→#: proxy exceptions do not include 127.0.0.1, so a configured proxy would hide a
  62→#: running demo from the launcher.
  63→_opener = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.ProxyHandler({}))
  64→
  65→RUNNING = "Ryde demo running at {url}"
  66→STOP_HINT = "Close this window (or press Ctrl+C) to stop the demo."
  67→ALREADY_RUNNING = "The Ryde demo is already running at {url}. Opening it in your browser."
  68→NO_FREE_PORT = ("Ports {first} to {last} are all in use by other programs. "
  69→                "Close one of them, then open this file again.")
  70→OPEN_YOURSELF = "Could not open a browser. Open {url} yourself."
  71→PORT_TAKEN = "Port {port} was taken just as the demo started. Open this file again."
  72→
  73→
  74→def start_url(port: int) -> str:
  75→    """The start page's URL on 127.0.0.1."""
  76→    return "http://127.0.0.1:%d%s" % (port, START_PATH)
  77→
  78→
  79→def server_argv(port: int) -> list:
  80→    """The existing server's own arguments: the mock, and the chosen port."""
  81→    return ["--llm", "mock", "--port", str(port)]
  82→
  83→
  84→def _answer(url: str) -> Optional[Tuple[int, str]]:
  85→    """(status, Server header) for a GET, or None when the port did not answer.
  86→
  87→    Any failure to get an answer — refused, timed out, a listener that speaks
  88→    something that is not HTTP — reads as None, never as a status.
  89→    """
  90→    try:
  91→        with _opener.open(url, timeout=PROBE_TIMEOUT) as response:
  92→            return response.status, response.headers.get("Server", "")
  93→    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
  94→        return exc.code, exc.headers.get("Server", "")
  95→    except Exception:
  96→        return None
  97→
  98→
  99→def is_ryde_demo(port: int) -> bool:
 100→    """True only when GET /start/ answers 200 with the Ryde server banner.
 101→
 102→    Nothing listening, another program's 200, and the Ryde banner on a 404 are all
 103→    False: only the two together prove this port serves the demo.
 104→    """
 105→    answer = _answer(start_url(port))
 106→    return bool(answer and answer[0] == 200 and answer[1].startswith(SERVER_HEADER))
 107→
 108→
 109→def _is_free(port: int) -> bool:
 110→    """True when a TCP connect to 127.0.0.1:port is refused (nobody is listening)."""
 111→    try:
 112→        with socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port), timeout=CONNECT_TIMEOUT):
 113→            return False
 114→    except ConnectionRefusedError:
 115→        return True
 116→    except OSError:
 117→        # Not a refusal — something is there, or the probe could not tell. Skipping
 118→        # the port is the safe reading.
 119→        return False
 120→
 121→
 122→def pick_port(first: int, last: int) -> Tuple[Optional[int], bool]:
 123→    """The first usable port in [first, last], and whether the demo already runs on it.
 124→
 125→    Ports are walked in order. A port already serving the Ryde demo is reused. Any
 126→    other listener — HTTP or one that never answers — is skipped. The first port
 127→    whose TCP connect is refused is used. (None, False) when every port is taken.
 128→    """
 129→    for port in range(first, last + 1):
 130→        if is_ryde_demo(port):
 131→            return port, True
 132→        if _is_free(port):
 133→            return port, False
 134→    return None, False
 135→
 136→
 137→def _open(url: str) -> bool:
 138→    """Open url in the default browser. False when the browser refused or raised."""
 139→    try:
 140→        return bool(webbrowser.open(url))
 141→    except webbrowser.Error:
 142→        return False
 143→
 144→
 145→def open_when_ready(url: str, timeout: float = READY_TIMEOUT) -> None:
 146→    """Open url in the browser once it answers 200, or print it when that fails.
 147→
 148→    The server starts on the main thread after this waiter, so the page must not be
 149→    opened before the port answers. A server that never answers, and a browser that
 150→    refuses or raises, both print the URL so the demo is still reachable by hand.
 151→    """
 152→    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
 153→    while True:
 154→        answer = _answer(url)
 155→        if answer is not None and answer[0] == 200:
 156→            break
 157→        if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
 158→            print(OPEN_YOURSELF.format(url=url))
 159→            return
 160→        time.sleep(POLL_SECONDS)
 161→    if not _open(url):
 162→        print(OPEN_YOURSELF.format(url=url))
 163→
 164→
 165→def _port_range(raw: str) -> Tuple[int, int]:
 166→    """'FIRST-LAST' as argparse takes it, or exit 2."""
 167→    first, sep, last = raw.partition("-")
 168→    if sep != "-":
 169→        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("ports must be FIRST-LAST, e.g. 8000-8010")
 170→    try:
 171→        first_port, last_port = int(first), int(last)
 172→    except ValueError:
 173→        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("ports must be FIRST-LAST, e.g. 8000-8010")
 174→    if not 1 <= first_port <= last_port <= 65535:
 175→        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("ports must be an increasing range within 1..65535")
 176→    return first_port, last_port
 177→
 178→
 179→def main(argv: Optional[list] = None) -> int:
 180→    """Pick a port, open the start page, and run the existing server. Returns its code."""
 181→    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
 182→        prog="python3 tools/launch.py",
 183→        description="Start the Ryde demo on the first free port and open the start page.",
 184→    )
 185→    parser.add_argument(
 186→        "--ports",
 187→        type=_port_range,
 188→        default=(FIRST_PORT, LAST_PORT),
 189→        metavar="FIRST-LAST",
 190→        help="ports to try, in order (default: %(default)s)",
 191→    )
 192→    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
 193→    first, last = args.ports
 194→
 195→    port, already_running = pick_port(first, last)
 196→    if port is None:
 197→        print(NO_FREE_PORT.format(first=first, last=last))
 198→        return 1
 199→
 200→    url = start_url(port)
 201→    if already_running:
 202→        print(ALREADY_RUNNING.format(url=url))
 203→        if not _open(url):
 204→            print(OPEN_YOURSELF.format(url=url))
 205→        return 0
 206→
 207→    print(RUNNING.format(url=url))
 208→    print(STOP_HINT)
 209→    # The waiter must not run before the server, so it goes on a daemon thread and the
 210→    # server keeps the main thread: Ctrl+C reaches app.server's own handler, and a
 211→    # closed terminal window ends this one process and frees the port.
 212→    threading.Thread(target=open_when_ready, args=(url,), daemon=True).start()
 213→    try:
 214→        return server.main(server_argv(port))
 215→    except OSError as exc:
 216→        # Two quick double-clicks can both pick the same free port; the loser's bind
 217→        # fails with EADDRINUSE. That is a race, not a bug: say so in one line, and
 218→        # the next double-click reuses the winner or takes the next free port.
 219→        if exc.errno in (errno.EADDRINUSE, 10048):
 220→            print(PORT_TAKEN.format(port=port))
 221→            return 1
 222→        raise
 223→
 224→
 225→if __name__ == "__main__":
 226→    sys.exit(main())
 227→

This package is a private teammate rehearsal source copy, not an online demo link or public-release clearance. It starts the existing Ryde dispute-resolution system locally with the real Tencent AI provider when the operator supplies private access through a sidecar.

## Extract and prepare

1. Extract the ZIP first. Keep the single top-level folder intact so `MANIFEST.json` stays beside the source tree.
2. Use Python 3.9 or newer. The runtime is standard-library-only; no installer or package download is needed.
3. The live run needs internet access to reach Tencent AI. It does not need CodeBuddy at runtime.
4. Receive `.env.live` through the agreed private credential channel and place it at the package root. It must contain the three role app keys, one each for the rider advocate, driver advocate and judge. The optional endpoint line is accepted only when it is the reviewed Tencent ADP destination. Never paste keys into a command line, a recording, a screenshot, a public issue or a source file.

The live launcher validates the UTF-8 sidecar before startup and refuses missing, blank, placeholder, duplicated or unsupported assignments. The standard `start.command` and `start.bat` remain the keyless mock entry points. They are useful when no private sidecar is available. The live entry points are `start-live.command` and `start-live.bat`; they explicitly select Tencent and never fall back to the mock.

## Start the local copy

On macOS, double-click `start-live.command`. If Finder warns about the script, use the narrow, local remedy **Open Anyway** in the file's context menu or Privacy & Security prompt; do not weaken global security settings. From a terminal, the equivalent manual command is:

```sh
python3 tools/launch_live.py
```

On Windows, double-click `start-live.bat`. It tries `py -3`, then `python`, and checks for Python 3.9 or newer. If Windows shows its script warning, use the file-specific **Run anyway** choice only after confirming that the ZIP came through the agreed private channel; do not change a machine-wide policy. The launcher changes to the package folder, so paths containing spaces remain usable.

The terminal owns the server process. Keep it open while filming or rehearsing; Ctrl+C stops the server and frees its port. Closing a browser tab does not stop it. The default live port is 8030, and an explicit port or credentials path can be supplied manually:

```sh
python3 tools/launch_live.py --credentials /private/path/.env.live --port 8030
```

The launcher prints the actual party page, operator-console URL and party status URL. It opens the party page only after its own loopback server answers. If the browser cannot be opened, use the printed URLs manually. A port already in use is refused rather than reused. The private sidecar is not printed in startup errors.

The mock route remains available for a keyless check:

```sh
python3 tools/launch.py
```

Do not describe that mock check as a live Tencent run. The live launcher is the only route in this copy that selects the real provider, and a decision record does not transfer money.

## Rehearsal handoff

Use synthetic inputs only. Coordinate one live caller at a time across machines, keep each run reference and its provider evidence, and preserve the local `runs/` directory across restarts. Real model waits can be several seconds per agent; provider errors are possible and must be reported as they occurred. Do not replace a failed live result with mock output or narrate a planned ending.

The agreed pair is one no-show rehearsal and one above-cap rehearsal using the supplied sample trips. Keep to the agreed two-rehearsal-filing allowance; do not invite unlimited retries or silently broaden it. The above-cap case demonstrates the human-review gate. If the real result differs from the filming narrative, stop for the operator and record the difference rather than changing the case, policy or outcome.

The accepted recording script is `drafts/w26/demo-script.md`, target 6:30, and it is a separate teammate handoff. `tools/deployment/demo-video-script.md` is an included source file in the complete-source ZIP; it is an older build-repository script, not approval to use its 7:25 timing. Settle the filming edit before production footage. Never film credentials or account consoles.

## Package and release boundaries

The packager selects a committed Git revision, records included and excluded source entries in `MANIFEST.json`, and preserves the executable macOS wrapper and Windows CRLF bytes. A `rehearsal` package is private. A `submission` package still waits for the separate release scrub, history and secret checks, verified access, approved private credential channel and any required form fields. The pattern scan is narrow and is not proof that no real key exists; the parent-owned gate compares against the ACTUAL live key bytes. No package, instruction or manifest contains an actual key.
"}

 112→        return "trailing dot or space"
 113→    if any(char in component for char in '<>:"|?*'):
 114→        return "a character not portable to Windows"
 115→    stem = component.split(".", 1)[0].rstrip(" .").upper()
 116→    if stem in RESERVED_WINDOWS_NAMES:
 117→        return "a reserved Windows name"

 121→def _portable_path_reason(path: str) -> Optional[str]:
 122→    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
 123→        return "empty path"
 124→    if "\\" in path:
 125→        return "backslash"
 126→    if path.startswith("/"):
 127→        return "absolute path"
 128→    if re.match(r"^[A-Za-z]:", path):
 129→        return "drive name"
 130→    if "\x00" in path or any(ord(char) < 32 or ord(char) == 127 for char in path):
 131→        return "control character"
 132→    if "//" in path:
 133→        return "repeated separator"
 134→    parts = path.split("/")
 135→    if any(part in ("", ".", "..") for part in parts):
 136→        return "dot or empty path component"
 137→    for part in parts:
 138→        reason = _portable_component_reason(part)
 139→        if reason is not None:
 140→            return reason
 141→    return None

 144→def _credential_path_reason(path: str) -> Optional[str]:
 145→    normal = path.replace("\\", "/")
 146→    lower = normal.lower()
 147→    parts = lower.split("/")
 148→    base = parts[-1] if parts else ""
 149→    if base == ".env.example":
 150→        return None
 151→    if base == ".env" or base.startswith(".env."):
 152→        return "live credential sidecar"
 153→    if "secrets" in parts:
 154→        return "credential store"
 155→    if lower == ".codebuddy/settings.local.json" or lower.endswith("/.codebuddy/settings.local.json"):
 156→        return "local credential settings"
 157→    if base in ("credentials.json", "auth.json") or base.startswith("credentials."):
 158→        return "credential store"
 159→    if base.endswith((".pem", ".key", ".p12", ".pfx")):
 160→        return "key material"
 161→    if base in ("id_rsa", "id_ed25519"):
 162→        return "private key material"
 163→    return None

 166→def _env_example_has_value(data: bytes) -> bool:
 167→    try:
 168→        text = data.decode("utf-8")
 169→    except UnicodeDecodeError:
 170→        return True
 171→    for raw_line in text.splitlines():
 172→        line = raw_line.strip()
 173→        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
 174→            continue
 175→        if line.startswith("export "):
 176→            line = line[len("export "):].strip()
 177→        if "=" not in line:
 178→            continue
 179→        key, value = line.split("=", 1)
 180→        if key.strip().upper() in ROLE_KEY_NAMES and value.strip():
 181→            return True
 182→    return False

 185→def content_refusals(path: str, data: bytes) -> List[str]:
 186→    """Return narrow, value-free findings for one Git blob."""
 187→    findings: List[str] = []
 188→    lower = path.replace("\\", "/").lower()
 189→    base = lower.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
 190→    if base == ".env.example" and _env_example_has_value(data):
 191→        findings.append("non-empty value in an environment example")
 192→    if data.startswith(b"version ") and b"git-lfs.github.com/spec/v1" in data[:256]:
 193→        findings.append("Git LFS pointer")
 194→    if re.search(rb"AKID[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}", data):
 195→        findings.append("Tencent SecretId-shaped content")
 196→    if re.search(rb"AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}", data):
 197→        findings.append("AWS access-key-shaped content")
 198→    if re.search(rb"-----BEGIN [A-Z0-9 ]*PRIVATE KEY-----", data):
 199→        findings.append("private-key-shaped content")
 200→    if re.search(rb"(?i)authorization[ \t]*:[ \t]*bearer[ \t]+\S+", data):
 201→        findings.append("bearer-token-shaped content")
 202→    return findings

 205→def _casefold_collisions(paths: List[str]) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
 206→    first: Dict[str, str] = {}
 207→    collisions: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []
 208→    for path in paths:
 209→        key = path.casefold()
 210→        if key in first and first[key] != path:
 211→            collisions.append((first[key], path))
 212→        else:
 213→            first[key] = path
 214→    return collisions

 217→def _junk_reason(path: str) -> Optional[str]:
 218→    lower = path.lower()
 219→    base = lower.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
 220→    if base == ".ds_store":
 221→        return "OS junk"
 222→    if base.startswith("~$"):
 223→        return "editor lock"
 224→    if lower.startswith("runs/") or "/runs/" in lower:
 225→        return "run output"
 226→    if lower.startswith("__pycache__/") or "/__pycache__/" in lower or base.endswith(".pyc"):
 227→        return "Python cache"
 228→    if lower.startswith(".pytest_cache/") or "/.pytest_cache/" in lower:
 229→        return "test cache"
 230→    if lower == ".codebuddy/settings.json" or lower.startswith(".codebuddy/"):
 231→        return "local CodeBuddy settings"

 235→def classify(entry: TreeEntry) -> Tuple[str, str]:
 236→    path_reason = _portable_path_reason(entry.path)
 237→    if path_reason is not None:
 238→        return "refuse", "unsafe path (%s)" % path_reason
 239→    credential_reason = _credential_path_reason(entry.path)
 240→    if credential_reason is not None:
 241→        return "refuse", credential_reason
 242→    junk_reason = _junk_reason(entry.path)
 243→    if junk_reason is not None:
 244→        return "exclude", junk_reason
 245→    if entry.kind != "blob" or entry.mode not in ("100644", "100755", "120000"):
 246→        return "refuse", "unsupported Git entry mode or type"
 247→    return "include", "source"

 250→def _symlink_target(path: str, data: bytes) -> str:
 251→    try:
 252→        target = data.decode("utf-8")
 253→    except UnicodeDecodeError:
 254→        raise PackageRefusal("%s: symlink target is not UTF-8" % path) from None
 255→    if not target or "\x00" in target or "\\" in target:
 256→        raise PackageRefusal("%s: symlink target is unsafe" % path)
 257→    if target.startswith("/"):
 258→        raise PackageRefusal("%s: symlink points outside the package root" % path)
 259→    resolved = posixpath.normpath(posixpath.join(posixpath.dirname(path), target))
 260→    if resolved == ".." or resolved.startswith("../"):
 261→        raise PackageRefusal("%s: symlink points outside the package root" % path)
 262→    return resolved

 265→def _validate_symlinks(records: Dict[str, Tuple[TreeEntry, bytes]]) -> None:
 266→    paths = set(records)
 267→    links: Dict[str, str] = {}
 268→    for path, (entry, data) in records.items():
 269→        if entry.mode != "120000":
 270→            continue
 271→        target = _symlink_target(path, data)
 272→        if target not in paths and not any(name.startswith(target + "/") for name in paths):
 273→            raise PackageRefusal("%s: symlink target is not in the package root" % path)
 274→        links[path] = target
 275→
 276→    def visit(path: str, stack: Tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
 277→        if path not in links:
 278→            return
 279→        if path in stack:
 280→            raise PackageRefusal("%s: symlink loop" % path)
 281→        visit(links[path], stack + (path,))
 282→
 283→    for path in links:
 284→        visit(path, ())

 287→def _output_raw_reason(raw: str) -> Optional[str]:
 288→    if "\\" in raw:
 289→        return "backslash"
 290→    if re.match(r"^[A-Za-z]:", raw):
 291→        return "drive name"
 292→    if "\x00" in raw or any(ord(char) < 32 or ord(char) == 127 for char in raw):
 293→        return "control character"
 294→    for component in raw.replace("\\", "/").split("/"):
 295→        if not component or component in (".", ".."):
 296→            continue
 297→        reason = _portable_component_reason(component)
 298→        if reason is not None:
 299→            return reason
 300→    return None

 303→def _same_disk_directory(left: Path, right: Path) -> bool:
 304→    try:
 305→        return os.path.isdir(str(left)) and os.path.samefile(str(left), str(right))
 306→    except (OSError, ValueError):
 307→        return False

 310→def _inside_repository(repo: Path, output_parent: Path) -> bool:
 311→    current = output_parent
 312→    while True:
 313→        if _same_disk_directory(current, repo):
 314→            return True
 315→        if current == current.parent:
 316→            return False
 317→        current = current.parent

 320→def _validate_output(repo: Path, raw_out: str, purpose: str, revision: str) -> Path:
 321→    reason = _output_raw_reason(raw_out)
 322→    if reason is not None:
 323→        raise PackageRefusal("unsafe output path (%s)" % reason)
 324→    output = Path(raw_out)
 325→    if not output.is_absolute():
 326→        output = Path.cwd() / output
 327→    if output.suffix.lower() != ".zip":
 328→        raise PackageRefusal("output filename must end in .zip")
 329→    marker = "ryde-live-%s-%s" % (purpose, revision[:12])
 330→    if marker not in output.name:
 331→        raise PackageRefusal("output filename does not contain the purpose and revision")
 332→    if not output.parent.exists():
 333→        raise PackageRefusal("output directory does not exist")
 334→    if not output.parent.is_dir():
 335→        raise PackageRefusal("output directory is not a directory")
 336→    if os.path.lexists(str(output)):
 337→        if output.is_symlink():
 338→            raise PackageRefusal("output path is a symlink")
 339→        raise PackageRefusal("output archive already exists")
 340→    if _inside_repository(repo, output.parent):
 341→        raise PackageRefusal("output is inside the repository")
 342→    return output

 345→def _wrapper_refusals(records: Dict[str, Tuple[TreeEntry, bytes]]) -> List[str]:
 346→    findings: List[str] = []
 347→    batch = records.get("start-live.bat")
 348→    if batch is not None:
 349→        entry, data = batch
 350→        if entry.mode != "100644":
 351→            findings.append("start-live.bat: expected Git mode 100644")
 352→        if not data or data.count(b"\n") != data.count(b"\r\n"):
 353→            findings.append("start-live.bat: expected CRLF line endings")
 354→    command = records.get("start-live.command")
 355→    if command is not None:
 356→        entry, data = command
 357→        if entry.mode != "100755":
 358→            findings.append("start-live.command: expected Git mode 100755")
 359→        if not data.startswith(b"#!/bin/bash\n") or b"\r" in data:
 360→            findings.append("start-live.command: expected executable Unix line endings")
 361→    return findings

 364→def _commit_datetime(repo: Path, revision: str) -> Tuple[Tuple[int, int, int, int, int, int], str]:
 365→    raw = _git(repo, "show", "-s", "--format=%ct", revision).strip()
 366→    try:
 367→        stamp = int(_decode(raw, "commit timestamp"))
 368→    except ValueError:
 369→        raise PackageRefusal("selected revision has no usable commit time") from None
 370→    moment = datetime.fromtimestamp(stamp, tz=timezone.utc)
 371→    return (
 372→        (moment.year, moment.month, moment.day, moment.hour, moment.minute, moment.second),
 373→        moment.isoformat(),
 374→    )

 377→def _zip_source_entry(archive: zipfile.ZipFile, name: str, data: bytes, mode: str,
 378→                      date_time: Tuple[int, int, int, int, int, int]) -> None:
 379→    info = zipfile.ZipInfo(name, date_time=date_time)
 380→    info.compress_type = zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED
 381→    if mode == "120000":
 382→        info.external_attr = 0o120777 << 16
 383→    else:
 384→        info.external_attr = int(mode, 8) << 16
 385→    info.create_system = 3
 386→    archive.writestr(info, data)

 389→def _build_archive(output: Path, top: str, records: Dict[str, Tuple[TreeEntry, bytes]],
 390→                   excluded: List[Dict[str, str]], manifest: Dict[str, object],
 391→                   date_time: Tuple[int, int, int, int, int, int]) -> None:
 392→    temporary = output.with_name("." + output.name + ".partial")
 393→    if os.path.lexists(str(temporary)):
 394→        raise PackageRefusal("temporary output path already exists")
 395→    try:
 396→        with zipfile.ZipFile(str(temporary), "w", compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as archive:
 397→            for path in sorted(records):
 398→                entry, data = records[path]
 399→                _zip_source_entry(archive, top + "/" + path, data, entry.mode, date_time)
 400→            manifest_data = (json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
 401→            _zip_source_entry(archive, top + "/MANIFEST.json", manifest_data, "100644", date_time)
 402→        try:
 403→            os.link(str(temporary), str(output))
 404→        except FileExistsError:
 405→            raise PackageRefusal("output archive already exists") from None
 406→        os.unlink(str(temporary))
 407→    except PackageRefusal:
 408→        if os.path.lexists(str(temporary)):
 409→            os.unlink(str(temporary))
 410→        raise
 411→    except Exception:
 412→        if os.path.lexists(str(temporary)):
 413→            os.unlink(str(temporary))
 414→        raise PackageRefusal("could not write the output archive") from None

 417→def _working_tree_dirty(repo: Path) -> bool:
 418→    return bool(_git(repo, "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=no"))
 419→
 420→
 421→def build(repo: Path, revision: str, purpose: str, raw_out: str) -> Path:
 422→    repo = Path(repo)
 423→    if not repo.is_dir():
 424→        raise PackageRefusal("repository directory does not exist")
 425→    resolved = _resolve_revision(repo, revision)
 426→    head = _resolve_revision(repo, "HEAD")
 427→    dirty = _working_tree_dirty(repo)
 428→    if dirty and resolved == head:
 429→        raise PackageRefusal("source revision is ambiguous because tracked files are modified")
 430→    output = _validate_output(repo, raw_out, purpose, resolved)
 431→    entries = _tree(repo, resolved)
 432→    by_path = {entry.path: entry for entry in entries}
 433→    missing = [path for path in REQUIRED_FILES if path not in by_path]
 434→    missing += [path for path in PRESERVED_FILES if path not in by_path]
 435→    if missing:
 436→        raise PackageRefusal("missing required package file or preserved source entry point: %s" %
 437→                             ", ".join(missing))
 438→
 439→    collisions = _casefold_collisions([entry.path for entry in entries])
 440→    if collisions:
 441→        detail = ", ".join("%s / %s" % pair for pair in collisions)
 442→        raise PackageRefusal("case-fold collision in source paths: %s" % detail)
 443→
 444→    records: Dict[str, Tuple[TreeEntry, bytes]] = {}
 445→    excluded: List[Dict[str, str]] = []
 446→    refusals: List[str] = []
 447→    for entry in sorted(entries, key=lambda item: item.path):
 448→        decision, reason = classify(entry)
 449→        if decision == "refuse":
 450→            refusals.append("%s (%s)" % (entry.path, reason))
 451→            continue
 452→        data = _blob(repo, entry.sha)
 453→        findings = content_refusals(entry.path, data)
 454→        if findings:
 455→            refusals.extend("%s (%s)" % (entry.path, finding) for finding in findings)
 456→            continue
 457→        if decision == "exclude":
 458→            excluded.append({"path": entry.path, "reason": reason})
 459→        else:
 460→            records[entry.path] = (entry, data)
 461→    if refusals:
 462→        raise PackageRefusal("unsafe source content or path: %s" % "; ".join(refusals))
 463→
 464→    wrapper_findings = _wrapper_refusals(records)
 465→    if wrapper_findings:
 466→        raise PackageRefusal("wrapper validation failed: %s" % "; ".join(wrapper_findings))
 467→    _validate_symlinks(records)
 468→
 469→    date_time, commit_iso = _commit_datetime(repo, resolved)
 470→    top = "ryde-live-%s-%s" % (purpose, resolved[:12])
 471→    included = []
 472→    for path in sorted(records):
 473→        entry, data = records[path]
 474→        included.append({
 475→            "path": path,
 476→            "git_mode": entry.mode,
 477→            "bytes": len(data),
 478→            "sha256": hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(),
 479→        })
 480→    manifest = {
 481→        "schema": "ryde-live-source-package-v1",
 482→        "source": {
 483→            "revision": resolved,
 484→            "revision_abbrev": resolved[:12],
 485→            "inventory": "Git tree blobs at the selected committed revision",
 486→            "commit_time": commit_iso,
 487→            "working_tree_dirty": dirty,
 488→        },
 489→        "package": {
 490→            "purpose": purpose,
 491→            "top_level_folder": top,
 492→            "built_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
 493→        },
 494→        "required_files": list(REQUIRED_FILES),
 495→        "included": included,
 496→        "excluded": excluded,
 497→        "counts": {"included": len(included), "excluded": len(excluded)},
 498→        "notes": {
 499→            "credentials": "The private .env.live is delivered separately and is never a source entry.",
 500→            "pattern_scan": "The narrow pattern scan is not proof that the archive contains no real credential.",
 501→            "w6_privacy_gate": "W6 privacy and release checks remain a parent-owned gate, including comparison against ACTUAL live key bytes.",
 502→        },
 503→    }
 504→    _build_archive(output, top, records, excluded, manifest, date_time)
 505→    print("Created %s" % output)
 506→    print("Extract the ZIP first, then run the launcher from the package folder.")
 507→    print("Copy the privately delivered .env.live beside the extracted source; do not put keys on a command line.")
 508→    print("Use start-live.command on macOS or start-live.bat on Windows; the standard start.command and start.bat remain mock entry points.")
 509→    print("The narrow pattern scan is not proof of a key-free archive; the release gate compares against ACTUAL live key bytes.")
 510→    return output
 511→
 512→
 513→def _parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
 514→    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
 515→        description="Package one committed Git source tree with no network call; this tool never reads, creates or rotates a credential.",
 516→    )
 517→    parser.add_argument("--repo", required=True, help="source repository directory")
 518→    parser.add_argument("--revision", required=True, help="explicit committed source revision")
 519→    parser.add_argument("--purpose", required=True, choices=("rehearsal", "submission"),
 520→                        help="package purpose")
 521→    parser.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="output ZIP path")
 522→    return parser
 523→
 524→
 525→def main(argv=None) -> int:
 526→    args = _parser().parse_args(argv)
 527→    try:
 528→        build(Path(args.repo), args.revision, args.purpose, args.out)
 529→    except PackageRefusal as exc:
 530→        print("REFUSED: %s" % exc)
 531→        return 1
 532→    return 0
 533→
 534→
 535→if __name__ == "__main__":
 536→    sys.exit(main())

   2→
   3→This package is a private teammate rehearsal source copy, not an online demo link or public-release clearance. It starts the existing Ryde dispute-resolution system locally with the real Tencent AI provider when the operator supplies private access through a sidecar.
   4→
   5→## Extract and prepare
   6→
   7→1. Extract the ZIP first. Keep the single top-level folder intact so `MANIFEST.json` stays beside the source tree.
   8→2. Use Python 3.9 or newer. The runtime is standard-library-only; no installer or package download is needed.
   9→3. The live run needs internet access to reach Tencent AI. It does not need CodeBuddy at runtime.
  10→4. Receive `.env.live` through the agreed private credential channel and place it at the package root. It must contain the three role app keys, one each for the rider advocate, driver advocate and judge. The optional endpoint line is accepted only when it is the reviewed Tencent ADP destination. Never paste keys into a command line, a recording, a screenshot, a public issue or a source file.
  11→
  12→The live launcher validates the UTF-8 sidecar before startup and refuses missing, blank, placeholder, duplicated or unsupported assignments. The standard `start.command` and `start.bat` remain the keyless mock entry points. They are useful when no private sidecar is available. The live entry points are `start-live.command` and `start-live.bat`; they explicitly select Tencent and never fall back to the mock.
  13→
  14→## Start the local copy
  15→
  16→On macOS, double-click `start-live.command`. If Finder warns about the script, use the narrow, local remedy **Open Anyway** in the file's context menu or Privacy & Security prompt; do not weaken global security settings. From a terminal, the equivalent manual command is:
